title: SCM: add version negotiation middleware + compatibility tests (client fallback to v1)
author: Jordan Lee
description: Implements SCM API version negotiation for /v1/cost-model/* endpoints (estimate + explain) and adds compatibility tests to ensure older clients remain functional as we introduce new SCM schema versions. This follows ADR-0147: negotiate via request headers (not path), keep responses self-describing, and allow graceful downgrade when the requested version is not supported. Behavior summary: Clients may send X-Redwood-SCM-Version (preferred version) and X-Redwood-SCM-Accept (comma-separated acceptable versions). Server selects the highest supported version from Accept; if only a preferred version is provided and it is unsupported, server returns v1 (if supported) and sets X-Redwood-SCM-Version: 1 plus X-Redwood-SCM-Negotiation: downgraded. If no version headers are provided, default to v1. If the client provides Accept and none overlap supported versions, return 406 UNSUPPORTED_VERSION with details including supported_versions and requested_versions. This PR also updates the internal CostModelClient to always send Accept ("1,2") and to parse response version headers; if v2 is requested but a downgrade occurs, the client logs a structured event (scm.version_downgrade) and continues using the returned payload. Includes unit tests for negotiation edge cases (missing headers, malformed Accept, duplicates, spacing, unknown versions) and integration/compat tests that run both the v1 JSON fixtures and v2-requested flows to confirm deterministic output equivalence when downgraded. No SCM v2 schema changes are introduced here; the v2 constant is treated as a "requested" value only to exercise negotiation and fallback paths.
